feed.title: Bartek Kus
feed.subtitle: Pragmatic full-stack engineer; identity; local-first infra; AI-assisted dev.

entry.title: Yolo mode is earned: three layers of Claude Code settings
entry.summary: I run Claude Code with permission prompts off. That is safe only because of what sits underneath: a global deny floor, project hooks as reflexes, and a config that is itself governed.

entry.title: Agentic code collapse, and the substrate that prevents it
entry.summary: Agent-built codebases have a characteristic failure mode: each diff is locally plausible while the system slides into incoherence. Receipts from a quarter-million governed lines on why mine hasn't.

entry.title: Inside spec-spine: a typed authority ledger over markdown
entry.summary: The governance spine underneath my platform: typed ownership edges, two deterministic registries, and a PR gate that refuses code drifting from its owning spec.

entry.title: Reading OWASP's Agentic Top 10 against a real platform
entry.summary: I mapped the OWASP ASI 2026 entries onto open-agentic-platform, control by control. The exercise kept landing on the same small set of governance mechanisms, and that is the finding.

entry.title: Production in the dev loop: Hetzner, Flux, and a read-only MCP
entry.summary: My Kubernetes cluster behaves like an extension of local development: the agent can see everything and touch nothing, and the only write path is git.

entry.title: Architecting intent vs vibe coding
entry.summary: AI can write the code; the unsolved problem is trusting what it wrote. Why review doesn't scale, and how specs-as-law makes agentic output governable.

entry.title: Probabilistic AI behind deterministic gates
entry.summary: LLMs are probabilistic by design; trustworthy systems are deterministic at the boundary. The architecture rule that makes agentic output admissible.

entry.title: Local-first, now governed
entry.summary: The local-first thesis grew a governance layer: why the agentic execution plane belongs on your machine, with no SaaS in the trust path.

entry.title: Identity in practice: OIDC, SSI, and DID without the hype
entry.summary: Practical guidance on when to use each identity standard, what to avoid, and links to authoritative specs.

entry.title: Design principles for resilient systems
entry.summary: Exploring simplicity, observability, blast radius, idempotency, and graceful degradation in distributed systems.

entry.title: RAG beyond the demo: failure modes and patterns
entry.summary: Exploring indexing strategies, chunking approaches, evaluation frameworks, observability, and guardrails for production RAG systems.
